narrative: Markets are grappling with broad-based equity de-risking as the US 10-year Treasury yield logs its longest streak above 5% since 2007. Persistent inflation has traders pricing in two to three additional Fed rate hikes, pressuring valuations across major benchmarks. While Anthropic's landmark upsized IPO demonstrated resilient appetite for pure-play AI, broader tech sentiment remains strained by expanding US export controls to China and surging AI compute and capital expenditures. Meanwhile, intensifying Middle East conflict—highlighted by US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island—is stoking supply risks against headwinds from slowing global demand. Gold and industrial metals are slumping heavily, hit by higher rate expectations and liquidity demands.

Nasdaq.why: Strong earnings and raised guidance from Nvidia alongside Anthropic's successful IPO offer support, but the index dropped roughly 2% as surging yields above 5% and expanding China export curbs pressure tech valuations.

S&P 500.why: The index suffered its broadest sell-off of the year, falling around 2% with over 450 constituents declining under the weight of higher-for-longer rate pricing and elevated yields.

Gold.why: Mark Cudmore and Abeer Abu Omar note gold is slumping sharply—dropping below $2,030/oz and trading down 12% YTD—weighed down by expectations of further US rate hikes and deleveraging.

Oil.why: Ziad Daoud flags upward supply-shock risks from Middle East conflict escalation near the Strait of Hormuz, yet Brent crude faces offsetting downward pressure from slowing global growth concerns.

priced_in: Two to three additional Federal Reserve interest rate hikes to address entrenched inflation
A higher-for-longer interest rate environment with elevated capital costs
Robust initial demand and valuation premiums for the Anthropic IPO
Nvidia's strong revenue beat and Q4 outlook reaffirming data center growth
Zero data center revenue from China for Nvidia due to export restrictions
debates: Sustainability of massive corporate AI capital expenditures and rising compute costs relative to revenue growth
Drivers behind the slump in gold and copper despite front-end yield moves, whether due to China demand weakness or IPO liquidity needs (Mark Cudmore)
Oil price trajectory balancing geopolitical supply shocks in the Strait of Hormuz versus global economic growth concerns
Tech index resilience: whether strong fundamentals from Nvidia and Anthropic can outweigh macro pressure from 5%+ Treasury yields
watch_next: Ongoing quarterly corporate earnings reports across tech and consumer sectors
December central bank policy meetings (Fed, ECB, BOJ)
